summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and a history of steal syndrome presented with inability to tolerate dialysis due to severe generalized body aches. He had previously undergone banding of his left brachiocephalic AV fistula without symptom relief. After admission, he underwent ligation of the fistula to address ongoing steal syndrome. He successfully completed two full dialysis sessions post-procedure without pain. Chronic pain from diabetic neuropathy persisted, prompting consultation with palliative care and initiation of nortriptyline. Oxycodone was increased, citalopram was uptitrated, and plans were made for outpatient follow-up with neurology, palliative care, and eye specialists. He was discharged to an extended care facility on his prior dialysis regimen via tunnelled catheter with instructions to monitor weight and symptoms.
